s: Seit über 150 Jahren rätseln Ornithologen darüber, wieso Brieftauben immer so zielsicher ihren Weg nach Hause finden.

nach Hause.et: From nach (“to”) + Hause, old dative of Haus (“house”).

s: in a short while (in the near future, but not more than a few hours)

to do (something) at a later time than planned, on a rescheduled date; to make up, catch up (on)

to get, fetch (someone or something) at another time or one more time

Er ist zum Buffet gegangen und hat sich noch was nachgeholt.

nachholen.et: 17th century, from nach- + holen, literally “to fetch [something] after”.

s: to yearn for (something in one's past)
Es hat keinen Sinn, den alten Zeiten nachzuhängen.
There's no point yearning for the past.
the act of catching up (on) or making up something

a rescheduled game, a match that had been postponed (e.g. due to icy conditions)
Nachholspiel.et: From nachholen (“to do something on a rescheduled date, to catch up”) + Spiel (“game, match”).
